title: W. H. DAVIS
text:
W. H. DAVIS.

It has been said that there is a grocery store for every family in town. While that is an exaggeration, the town has a goodly number of first class groceries. Among this number is W. H. Davis. He has been here only a few years and his stock is new and clean, hence, he holds his customers by giving them pure goods and the newest things on the market. Mr. Davis is also the city tinner and hardware dealer, and the same straightforward methods p[rev]ail in these departments, and his attentive clerk assists him greatly in keeping up his trade. Mr. Davis is an old [t]ime Savoy boy and has such a [ple]asant disposition that he wins [cus]tomers and holds them.
notes: Left edge of clipping slightly cut; a few words reconstructed in brackets. This appears to be a business profile/advertisement from an early Savoy publication.
